date.as_written: netragotragirau varṣe mādhave prathame site | dvādaśyāṃ śanivāre ... samva(!) 772 naṣṭavaiṣākhaśu(kla)dvādaśī

notes: The chronogram 'netragotragirau' gives 772 when read right to left: giri = 7, gotra (the seven kulaparvatas) = 7, netra = 2. This matches the numerals 'samva 772' and the catalogue's NS 772, which works out to 1652 CE. The verse calls the month 'prathama mādhava' (first Vaiśākha), so this was probably a year with an intercalary Vaiśākha. The Newari colophon calls it 'naṣṭavaiṣākha', and the exact meaning of 'naṣṭa' there is unclear. The Newari passage 'kuhnu svanihma śrīdevadāsadevayākāṃ' is obscure. 'kuhnu' means 'on that day'. 'svanihma' might be a garbled 'svanigahma', meaning 'a person of Svanigaḥ (Kathmandu)', but this is uncertain, so it is not recorded as a residence. I read '-yākāṃ' as marking the person for whom the scribe wrote, which gives Devadāsadeva the role of commissioner or beneficiary with medium confidence. Jagaddhara is the author of the commentary Rasadīpinī on the Meghadūta, not of the Meghadūta itself.
